papers.title: Linear Axiomatization of Linear Differential Equations
papers.abstract: This article presents an axiomatization of linear differential equations that is complete for topologically open properties with compact initial conditions and time horizons by proving them deductively via a sound reduction to formulas of linear real arithmetic. Indeed, linearity is preserved: linear differential invariants are complete for open properties of linear differential equations and reduce with a linear number of Lie derivatives (per atom) to linear real arithmetic. In particular, this article shows that the linear fragment of differential dynamic logic (dL), a modal extension of standard first-order logic over the reals satisfies these completeness properties. By establishing completeness within decidable linear real arithmetic, the need for proving sophisticated nonlinear formulas of real arithmetic is circumvented. Furthermore, this article establishes generalizations to the nonlinear fragment of dL that enable the practical certification of reachability computations, validating the output of external computations in dL with machine-checkable proofs.

papers.title: Computable Quantification in Reflective Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Informal statements of G\"odel's incompleteness theorems often run: "any consistent formal system with arithmetic has true but unprovable statements." That reading assumes a classical notion of truth, under which a universal statement is true as soon as each of its numeral instances is. This paper presents reflective grounded arithmetic (RGA), in which truth is grounded in computation and universal quantification is grounded reflectively: a universal statement is true when the system's own proof search certifies its schematic instance, and false when the system refutes one numeral instance. RGA allows recursive definitions without restriction and proves addition, multiplication and Ackermann's function total as theorems quantified inside the system. RGA is consistent, and it is complete for its own, grounded notion of truth: every well-formed statement that evaluates to true is provable. G\"odel's theorems still hold for RGA, as a companion paper shows. The statements that classical reasoning calls true but unprovable have every numeral instance provable but no certified schematic instance, so they are ungrounded in RGA; read instance by instance, in an $\omega$-semantics for which RGA is also sound, they are true. All results are machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL: soundness and consistency; completeness for grounded truth, open statements included; $\omega$-soundness and $\omega$-consistency; that grounded truth is recursively enumerable and RGA represents exactly the recursively enumerable sets; and $\omega$-incompleteness. The logic is neither classical nor intuitionistic: double negation is eliminable as an entailment, excluded middle fails wherever a statement has no boolean value, RGA has the disjunction and witness properties, and the deduction theorem holds exactly at provably decided hypotheses.

papers.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
papers.abstract: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.

papers.title: Computational techniques for sheaf cohomology of locally profinite sets
papers.abstract: We compute the sheaf cohomology with constant $\mathbb{Z}_2$ coefficients of a concrete class of locally profinite sets of independent interest. We introduce $k$-sheer partitions to aid in constructions. It is also shown that questions of intermediate cohomology degrees can be reduced to questions about top cohomology degrees by exhibiting nontrivial top cocycles as pointwise limits of coboundaries.

papers.title: Big Ramsey degrees and structures in relational languages
papers.abstract: We establish a precompact transfer theorem for big Ramsey structures and a uniform envelope theorem for valuation hypergraphs. These yield big Ramsey structures for generic injective relational structures in languages with finitely many symbols of each positive arity, answering the existence part of Problem~6.3.2 of Balko et al.\ [M.~Balko et al., J.~Eur.~Math.~Soc.\ 28, 2101--2150 (2026)], and refute Conjecture~4.7 of Braunfeld et al.\ [S.~Braunfeld et al., Adv.~Comb., Paper No.~4 (2024)]. We also construct a finitely constrained free amalgamation class in a finite language of maximum arity three whose Fra\"iss\'e limit has infinite singleton big Ramsey degree, giving a negative answer to the existence question in Problem~6.3.3 of Balko et al.

papers.title: Hyperwellfoundedness and Eventual Domination
papers.abstract: We prove that a Borel strict partial order is an increasing union of wellfounded Borel partial orders if and only if it admits an (injective) Borel homomorphism to the eventual domination order.

papers.title: The first-order part of the Ordered Variable Word theorem
papers.abstract: An ordered $\omega$-variable sequence over a finite alphabet~$A$ is an infinite sequence over the extended alphabet $A \sqcup \{ x_0, x_1, \dots \}$, where each variable kind appears at least once, and the last occurrence of $x_i$ appears before the first occurrence of $x_{i+1}$. The Ordered Variable Word theorem states that for every finite coloring of the words over a finite alphabet~$A$, there is an ordered $\omega$-variable sequence~$W$ over~$A$ such that every word induced by substituting variables with letters, and cutting before the first undefined variable, has the same color. In this article, we prove that the Ordered Variable Word theorem is $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$. It follows that the tree theorem for singletons by Chubb, Hirst, and McNicholl is $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$, answering a long-standing open question. Lemma 3.13 was found by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic).

papers.title: SEAC from EAC modulo Schanuel: reduction to algebraic exponentials
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of reducing Zilber's pseudo-exponentiation conjecture to mere exponential-algebraic closedness, assuming Schanuel's conjecture but not Zilber-Pink. Generalising work of Mantova, we show that it would suffice to show that perfectly rotund varieties have non-dense intersection with finitely generated subgroups of the graph of exponentiation in which the exponentials live in a number field.

papers.title: There can be equitable social welfare orders but no fair voting system
papers.abstract: In the context of intergenerational equity it is natural to ask that social welfare orders have th properties of finite anonymity and strong Pareto efficiency. Such social welfare orders can be constructed from nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers, and the existence of ultrafilters of this kind is known to be equivalent to the existence of a fair voting system for a countably infinite population in the sense of Arrow's theorem. Unfortunately, the existence of this variety of social welfare order, which we call anonymous Pareto, implies the existence of nonmeasurable sets of real numbers. For some, such as Litak, this entails that such social welfare orders are inadmissible for use in theoretical economics because they are non-constructive in nature. The authors seek to give nuance to this view, proving that anonymous Pareto and other social welfare orders can exist in the absence of nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers.

papers.title: Closed maximal eventually different families for $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^0_3$ and weakly Farah ideals
papers.abstract: Motivated by the existence of closed maximal $\mathcal{I}$-eventually different ($\mathcal{I}$-MED) families, we study uniform combinatorial properties of ideals. For a fixed ideal, a property is uniform if its witnesses can be chosen by a single Borel map. We prove that every $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^0_3$ ideal is uniformly weakly $P^+$. We also prove that the classes of Farah and weakly Farah ideals coincide, answering a question of Hru\v{s}\'ak and Meza-Alc\'antara. We then show that every weakly Farah ideal is uniformly weakly Ramsey. As an application, we obtain closed $\mathcal{I}$-MED families for $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^0_3$ ideals and weakly Farah ideals.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Monotone Completeness Conjecture
papers.abstract: Combining a modification of the recent counterexample to the quasitrace conjecture with model-theoretic reductions due to the first author, we exhibit a counterexample to the monotone completeness conjecture. We fully reproduce the disproof of the quasitrace conjecture by a modified construction and arguments.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
papers.abstract: This is the first of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on stability. An observable is stable when the order in which the two systems are idealized never changes its expectation value, and this is Shelah's stability. Its classical characterizations, in model theory and in analysis, acquire a physical meaning: idealized preparations are simulated by finite mixtures of actual ones, and adaptive probes can tell apart only polynomially many preparations.

papers.title: Finite Combinatorics and Fragments of Arithmetic
papers.abstract: In fragments of first order arithmetic, definable maps on finite domains could behave very differently from finite maps. Here combinatorial properties of $\Sigma_{n+1}$-definable maps on finite domains are compared in the absence of $B\Sigma_{n+1}$. It is shown that $\mathrm{GPHP}(\Sigma_{n+1})$ (the $\Sigma_{n+1}$-instance of Kaye's General Pigeonhole Principle) lies strictly between $\mathrm{CARD}(\Sigma_{n+1})$ and $\mathrm{WPHP}(\Sigma_{n+1})$ (Weak Pigeonhole Principle for $\Sigma_{n+1}$-maps), and also that $\mathrm{FRT}(\Sigma_{n+1})$ (Finite Ramsey's Theorem for $\Sigma_{n+1}$-maps) does not imply $\mathrm{WPHP}(\Sigma_{n+1})$.

papers.title: Dilator-based analysis of KP
papers.abstract: Proof theorists developed various frameworks to analyze impredicative systems like $\Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{CA}_0$ or $\mathsf{KP}$; One is an operator-controlled derivation system, and the other is Girard's dilator-based $\beta$-logic. In this paper, we provide a functorial formulation of operator-controlled analysis of $\mathsf{KP}$, thereby unifying the two approaches into a single framework. As an application, a new proof of Girard's boundedness theorem is also provided, which states that every $\Sigma_1$-over-$L_{\omega_1^{\mathsf{CK}}}$-definable function $\omega_1^\mathsf{CK}\to \omega_1^\mathsf{CK}$ is bounded by a recursive dilator.

papers.title: A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture
papers.abstract: Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture. This answers a long-standing open question of Hart, Kim and Pillay (1996).

papers.title: On the foundations of logic and probability, II. Modal probability spaces
papers.abstract: A class of models which brings to the fore the inner logic of the calculus of probability instead of assigning probabilities to sentences is introduced and investigated.

papers.title: Functional Projection and Complexity Reduction
papers.abstract: T\"ornquist (arXiv:1310.3250) proved that if there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_2$ maximal almost disjoint (MAD) family, then there exists a $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$ MAD family. Since then, several other "complexity reduction" proofs have been found for other combinatorial objects, such as maximal independent families or ultrafilters. All of these proofs have relied on $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$-uniformization, so they did not easily lift to higher projective levels. In this paper, we introduce a principle weaker than Uniformization which we call "Functional Projection", and show that this principle is sufficient for most complexity reduction proofs. On the other hand, we prove that in $L[U]$, the canonical inner model for a measurable cardinal, Functional Projection holds for $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ relations. As an immediate corollary, we obtain that in $L[U]$ there are $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_2$ witnesses for many combinatorial families.
